page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_v3 belongs to the memory-optimized MBDSv3 family, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating up to 4.0 GHz. Memory capacity totals 768 GB, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation alongside a 105 MB L3 cache. The x86_64 architecture incorporates vector extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix instructions. Local storage is provisioned via a bundled 429 GB solid-state drive, while no hardware GPUs are present.

Benchmark testing reveals robust parallel computation and data throughput capabilities. The multi-core stress-ng metric reaches 90,931.06, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,551.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 97,410.84. Memory bandwidth achieves 429.08 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 184.62 GB/sec in large-block write operations, reflecting substantial bus throughput. In application-level benchmarks, the instance recorded 34,663.21 on PassMark database operations, 118.21 million Redis SET operations per second, and 111.84 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 positions the M96bds_v3 for scale-up in-memory data processing, large relational databases, and enterprise caching layers. While multi-threaded execution and vector-driven matrix computations perform exceptionally well, single-core CPU metrics sit closer to median distributions. The inclusion of 429 GB local SSD storage supports fast ephemeral scratch data, though extensive non-volatile persistence requires attached block storage. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-heavy enterprise database engines, complex analytical modeling, and in-memory caches that fully exploit its dense memory pool and 96 dedicated threads.
description: Microsoft Azure M96bds_v3 is a memory-optimized cloud server built for data-dense and parallel compute environments. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs from a 48-core Intel Xeon 8473C processor clocked at 4.0 GHz, backed by 768 GB of system memory and 105 MB of L3 cache. The x86_64 CPU configuration includes advanced AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions, supported by a bundled 429 GB local SSD without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional memory throughput, reaching 429.08 GB/sec for large uncached reads, along with high PassMark database operational scores and 118.21 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread CPU performance operates within median ranges, the instance delivers high multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth. It is tailored for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, enterprise data warehousing, and high-throughput static data delivery.
